rows.description: CRA Board, Dec 2: vote on funding to the City to buy the S&P Mobile Home Park (west of the County Administration complex). City Commission ratified the purchase contract Nov 16; staff memo says the owner set a $9M price and would not negotiate. CRA share and purpose not stated.

CRA Board, Dec 1: Res. 01-2027, $3,000 mural matching grant to Downtown Stuart Retail, LLC, the property owner, for a mural on the north wall of its building at 37 SW Osceola St; CRA vote ahead (0.04% of Stuart's special revenue funds).

City Council, Oct 19: staff sought consensus to negotiate an incentive agreement with Hub Steel for up to $200,000 in building permit fee reimbursement for a manufacturing expansion, paid from the Building Fund and/or General Fund; final agreement returns to Council (0.8% of general fund).
rows.shortfall: Interim City Manager Maslow (Sept 28 minutes): about $16M ad valorem revenue, initial Amendment 3 reduction forecast about $3.5M

rows.description: BCC, Nov 16: MOU with Tallahassee contemplating County purchase of six city fire stations for $1.9M, leased back to the City for $1, once a new long-term master agreement is adopted; also contemplates higher FY2028 fire assessment and fee rates after a rate study.
rows.shortfall: Leon commissioners discussed deeper cuts after Amendment 3 (Tallahassee Democrat, Nov 13)

rows.description: City Council, Dec 3: three-year agreement, two one-year renewals, with Pier Events, LLC for events management services for the Enterprise Facilities Department, up to $860,000 for the initial term; vote ahead. Paying fund not stated.
City Council consent, Dec 3: $1,000,000 allocation increase for tanker pump-out services with Envirowaste Services Group, Inc. for the Water Resources Department; vote ahead. Paying fund not stated.
BCC, Nov 24: Blue Springs Phase 3A sewer extension (about 4,117 LF gravity main, 5,296 LF force main, 35 services); item text cites $4,281,765; funding source not shown in the excerpt; vote ahead.

BCC, Nov 24: award of bid 2627-02, milling and resurfacing Old US Road (CR 167), to low bidder Southeast Construction Company, LLC at $1,809,550.80 of 5 bids; FDOT funding of $3,469,324 covers it; vote ahead.

City Commission, Nov 24: Res. 2026-095, $1,354,231.30 contract with Southern Underground Industries, Inc. for the Tidal Valve Program; $1,000,000 EPA grant plus $354,231.30 from the Drainage Fund; vote ahead.

City Council, Nov 17: sole-source purchase of five Trackman golf simulator bays, $319,661, as an exception to purchasing policy; staff says the Okaloosa County TDC approved the funding. Same agenda: Toro autonomous range mower package, $150,678.49 in TDC funds. Outcome not verified.

OMNI CRA Board, Nov 19: by 4/5 vote, waives competitive bidding to pay Global Flow PR and More, Inc. up to $200,000 for a pilot of public art wraps and streetscape work on eight columns along NE 15th St (0.04% of Miami's special revenue funds). Outcome not verified.

BCC, Nov 18: $35,000 in one-time funding for the Florida vs. Florida State Legacy Weekend Tailgate and Watch Party, a Bradenton Area Convention and Visitors Bureau item (0.005% of general fund; paying fund not stated). Outcome not verified.
rows.shortfall: Chairman Tal Siddique: new parks, libraries "needs to just stop"; staff estimate $63M (Suncoast Searchlight, Nov 19)

rows.description: BCC, Nov 17: $8,650,040.88 contract with ECSC, LLC for Project Opal Bid Package No. 2 site improvements at the Shoal River Gigasite; a companion item names Project Opal as the Williams International Co, LLC economic development project. Funding source not stated. Outcome not verified.

SEOPW CRA Board, Nov 19: development agreement granting AMC HTG 2, Ltd. up to $1,000,000 from Series 2025 CRA bond proceeds for affordable housing; any excess funds returned to the CRA go back to the developer as an additional grant. Outcome not verified.

BCC, Nov 17: Community Human Service Partnership (CHSP) funding item, $1,445,000 per item text, pulled from consent; Commissioner Maddox recused, citing his position as CEO of Family Promise of the Big Bend. Recipients not listed in the excerpt. Outcome not verified.
rows.shortfall: Leon commissioners discussed deeper cuts after Amendment 3 (Tallahassee Democrat, Nov 13)

rows.description: City Commission, Nov 17: sole-source procurement from Packetalk, LLC, up to $500,000, waiving competitive procurement, for camera system expansion and a Real-Time Crime Center, funded by an FY26 federal COPS Technology and Equipment grant. Outcome not verified.

School Board special meeting, Nov 20: approval to complete the Royal Palm School partial renovation, up to $5,300,000 from capital millage; more funding may be needed outside the construction scope. Outcome not verified.
Nov 20 (Newsweek): Mayor Karen Love on the budget gap: "This is not going to be an easy discussion." City must cut $1.1M in services or raise $1.1M in revenue.

Nov 20 (WGCU/Suncoast Searchlight): County Administrator Jonathan Lewis paused hiring for 250 vacancies; memo tells outside partners to "plan for the potential of funding reduction." Projected loss $134M within two years.
rows.shortfall: Projected loss $134M in two years, $386.6M in five (FAC)

rows.description: WGCU/Suncoast Searchlight, Nov 20: "After Amendment 3, Sarasota County will review planned projects; Here's what they cost". Includes $84.8M sheriff HQ expansion, $20M Benderson Park sports complex share, $13.2M Longboat Key Library; review set for Dec 15.

rows.government: St. Pete Beach / Gulfport / St. Johns County
rows.description: Newsweek, Nov 20: "Florida officials cut back public services after Amendment 3 passes". Cites St. Pete Beach trolley cut, Gulfport $1.1M gap, and a paused $100M St. Johns County fire station project.

CRA, Dec 3: finds that disposing of the Deuces Rising Replat lots (Lots 1-12, Blocks 1 and 2, plus common tracts) at 2250 Fairfield Ave S and 23rd St S for less than fair value fits the South St. Pete CRA plan; recommends City Council approval. Buyer and price not stated.

BCC: Tourist Development Tax funding for marketing/promotional fees and related expenses for Discover Lake County to be designated a sponsor of Montverde Academy. Amount not stated. Outcome not verified. Dec 1 packet minutes show $250,000; Commr. Parks recused, citing a nonpaid advisory role with Montverde Academy.
